chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, is not a tyrant to His servant, but the servant is the one who tyrannizes himself.

key_terms.يَظْلِمُ نَفْسَهُ: He tyrannizes himself / He wrongs his own soul

ai.seo_question: Does God wrong His servants or do they wrong themselves?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this principle within the Shia doctrine of *Adl* (Divine Justice), emphasizing that afflictions are either expiations for minor sins or elevations in rank for the righteous, rather than arbitrary divine punishment. This aligns with the Mu'tazili-influenced Shia view that God is free from *Dhalim* (wrongdoing), attributing suffering to human *Zulm al-Nafs* (self-injustice) through negligence or sin.
